methods.summary: Delete every unused material and component definition, as one undo entry.

Revert to Saved: re-read the document's saved file in place, discarding every change since the last save. The undo and redo history is cleared and the document reads clean. Refuses `nothing_to_revert` when the document has no saved file or has no changes since the last save. There is no confirmation step: the caller is deliberate.

Save the attached document (Save / Save As) as .hew or SketchUp .skp: the file is written, the unsaved mark cleared, and the document bound to it. `copy` writes a copy without any of that. With no `path` it re-saves in place; a document with no file yet, in a host that cannot ask where, hands the bytes back instead.

copy.description: write a copy to `path` — the document is not rebound to it and keeps its unsaved mark; requires `path`

format.description: "skp" is the 2026 container (what current SketchUp saves), "skp2017" the 2017 format (opens in SketchUp Make 2017 and later). Absent: a .skp path keeps the working file's own .skp container (the 2026 one for a document that did not come from a .skp), any other path writes .hew, and no path uses the working file's own format. A format that contradicts the path's extension is refused (format_mismatch).

return_bytes.description: hand the document's bytes back and write nothing: no file, no binding, no saved mark; takes no `path`

units.description: The display units a SketchUp file opens in (hew.view.units's formats), a save back over a .skp included. Absent: a save back keeps the file's own units and a new file takes the host's display units (the app's preference live; meters headless). A .hew ignores it.

methods.summary: Draw an arc on a plane spec.

close.description: how the arc's ends are closed: "open" (default, a bare arc), "pie" (closed wedge — two radii to the center), or "segment" (closed circular segment — the chord). "pie"/"segment" commit a closed profile (a region in plane/sketch mode, a SplitFaceInner loop in face mode) like draw_rect/draw_circle, and need at least 2 segments (see "segments"). Must be "open" when the sweep is a full turn (already closed).

segments.description: facet count; defaults proportionally to the sweep, capped at MAX_CIRCLE_SEGMENTS = 1024. A single chord (1) is fine for close: "open", but close: "pie"/"segment" needs at least 2 — a single chord can't form a non-degenerate closed loop — and the proportional default is floored at 2 for those modes too.

units.description: unit keys from hew.sketch.units: isl_<hex16> (an island: all its edges), edg_<hex16> (one edge), crv_<hex16> (every facet of one circle), rgn_<hex16> (a region's ring edges that are drawing edges)

result.description: the plane units the edit made (new keys after the edit); empty for delete

units.description: the plane units the call touched: every drawing edge lying along what was drawn, then every region whose boundary carries it

key.description: edg_<hex16> or rgn_<hex16>, as hew.sketch.units lists them

object_id.description: the owning solid, for topology and owned

sketch_id.description: the sketch holding the drawing, for owned and free when it has one

store.description: topology: the solid's own face structure; owned: drawing kept on the solid's face; free: drawing over no face

methods.summary: List a plane's drawing as units: islands of edges (with where each is stored) and regions.

extrudable.description: true when the region lies over no face and hew.solid.extrude takes it as a new Object

face.description: a face locator ({object, at}) for the region when it IS a face of that solid — pass it to hew.solid.push_pull

object_id.description: the solid under the region, when one is

curve.description: present when the edge is a facet of an analytic circle

methods.summary: Close an open object's flat openings with faces; an object closed all round becomes a solid.

object.description: obj_ id (a world object or a component member)

rims.description: indices into the object's hew.doc.health rims; omitted = every cappable rim (when none is, all of them, so the refusal says why)

closed.description: the object is now a solid

faces.description: faces added (face tokens cap.1, cap.2, ... in a transaction)

reversed.description: an island the caps closed was inside out, so that island's faces were turned over (a cavity inside another island is left as is)

methods.summary: Remove faces from an open object; islands cut loose become objects of their own. Solids refuse.

faces.description: faces of that object; omitted = every face, which deletes the object (a component member too, unless it is its component's last object: last_definition_member)

deleted.description: every face went, so the object was deleted

object_ids.description: islands cut loose, now objects of their own

methods.summary: Kept for compatibility: delete a drawn shape (sub-face or chord island) back into its face; hew.sketch.delete is the general form.

imprint.description: HEW_API.md §5.2 face locator ({object,at} | {object,ray} | {"$face":"label#key"}) naming a sub-face; {object,at} also picks a CHORD when the point lies on one of its lines (a chord is tried first, then the sub-face containing the point)

methods.summary: Extrude a region into a new Object, consuming the profile.

plane.description: HEW_API.md §7 plane spec naming the drafting context a unit-key `region` belongs to. A region over no face extrudes as a new Object; a region that is a face of a solid push/pulls that face (result as hew.solid.push_pull); a region over a face that cannot hold it refuses region_not_pushable

region.description: a sketch region id; with `plane`, a region unit key rgn_<hex16> from hew.sketch.units

result.description: mints face tokens "base", "top", "side.<n>" (boundary-loop order) — HEW_API.md §5.4's normative example — when a new Object results

object_ids.description: a through-cut's resulting pieces (unit-key form over a face, as hew.solid.push_pull)

methods.summary: Sweep a profile along an edge-chain path, as the tool does.

oneOf.description: Reserved: no kernel mapping yet — refuses unimplemented

methods.summary: Kept for compatibility: list an object's drawn shapes (sub-faces and chords) per drawing plane; hew.sketch.units is the general form.

curve_units.description: drawn circles and arcs (whole or cut by other drawing into several runs) on the object's drawing planes: each {closed, curve: {center, radius}, runs: [{at, path}]}, a run that is a chord above carrying that chord's at locator — the whole drawn curve, a circle when closed, else an arc

at.description: sub_face: an interior point clear of any nested sub-face; chord: the midpoint of the run's first segment — the locator to pass to move_imprint/rotate_imprint/scale_imprint/delete_imprint

curve.description: sub_face only: {center, radius} when the whole loop is one drawn circle, else null

curves.description: per edge of the loop (sub_face) or run (chord), in order: {center, radius} when that edge is a facet of a drawn circle or arc, else null — a pie, segment, or edge-to-edge arc reports its arc here

holes.description: sub_face only: the hole loops' positions

loop.description: sub_face only: the outer loop's positions, cycle order

nested.description: sub_face only: count of sub-faces lying inside this one

path.description: chord only: the run's vertex positions, first to last

region.description: sub_face only: the region's unit key (rgn_…) on that plane, as hew.sketch.units reports it

unit.description: the island's unit key (isl_…) on that plane, as hew.sketch.units reports it

methods.summary: Boolean intersection of two solids.
Mark an open object as a surface on purpose (or clear the mark); hew.doc.health keeps listing it, flagged accepted.

methods.summary: Push/pull a face of a solid with the tool's full semantics.

result.description: exactly one of object_id / object_ids is present, depending on the tool's three-way branch (HEW_API.md §7 semantics notes)

object_id.description: the pushed/pulled object, still standing (in-place or sub-face case)

object_ids.description: a through-cut's resulting pieces, replacing the source object

methods.summary: Kept for compatibility: turn a drawn shape about its plane's normal through a pivot; hew.sketch.rotate is the general form.

imprint.description: HEW_API.md §5.2 face locator ({object,at} | {object,ray} | {"$face":"label#key"}) naming a sub-face; {object,at} also picks a CHORD when the point lies on one of its lines (a chord is tried first, then the sub-face containing the point)

methods.summary: Kept for compatibility: uniformly scale a drawn shape about an anchor in its plane; hew.sketch.scale is the general form.

methods.summary: Slice a solid by a plane into two solids.
Boolean subtraction of two solids.
Pull a flat surface into a solid of the given thickness.

centered.description: split the thickness evenly on both sides of the surface

distance.description: meters along each face's front normal (negative: behind it)

object_ids.description: further separate pieces of the surface, each now a solid of its own

Assign a tag to nodes.

Delete a tag path, unassigning it everywhere.

Set the live desktop viewport's camera. A host effect on the view, not a document edit (mutates_document = false: never recorded, never resyncs the document). Headless clients pass a camera per hew.view.snapshot call instead.

params.description: exactly one of camera or view is required

camera.description: mutually exclusive with view; identical vocabulary to hew.view.snapshot's camera

parallel_height.description: the height the view spans at the target, meters (what a parallel view frames); defaults to what the perspective view spans there

view.description: a named standard view; mutually exclusive with camera

methods.summary: Hidden-line drawing of the visible document from a camera (crates/hlr): hard edges, curved-wall silhouettes, section-cut outlines, optionally dashed hidden lines — as a true-size SVG at a drawing scale (inline or written to path), or as raw segments in view-plane meters.

camera.description: identical vocabulary to hew.view.snapshot's camera; mutually exclusive with view and scene

include_hidden.description: defaults to false; when true, hidden pieces are returned too (kind "hidden", dashed in SVG)

include_soft.description: defaults to false; when true, non-silhouette curved-wall facet seams are returned (kind "soft")

path.description: svg only: write the file here instead of returning it inline (hosts with filesystem access)

scale.description: svg only: paper/model drawing scale, defaults to 1 (full size); the SVG's width/height are millimeters at that scale

scene.description: a Scene's id: its camera and hidden sets, as hew.view.snapshot

view.description: a named standard view (parallel projection); mutually exclusive with camera and scene

bounds.description: [min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y] in view-plane meters; null when empty

ids.description: public id of the entity each segment belongs to

segments.description: format segments: [ax, ay, bx, by] in view-plane meters, y up, origin at the camera target

methods.summary: Render the attached document to PNG, headless-rendered via a software rasterizer (a live host may render through its viewport instead) — bytes base64 by default, or a path on hosts with filesystem access.

parallel_height.description: the height the view spans at the target, meters (what a parallel view frames); defaults to what the perspective view spans there

depth_bits.description: bits per pixel of the depth PNG (default 8); only with include_depth

height.description: defaults to 512; out-of-range values are clamped, not refused

include_depth.description: defaults to false; when true, also returns a depth pass as a grayscale PNG — NEAR is WHITE, background 0 — with depth_near/depth_far (meters from the eye along the view axis) so absolute depth is recoverable: depth = depth_far - (v - 1) / (max - 1) * (depth_far - depth_near), max = 255 or 65535. The conditioning input depth-aware image models expect

include_ids.description: defaults to false; when true, also returns a per-pixel id-buffer and its palette

include_normals.description: defaults to false; when true, also returns a camera-space normals pass as an RGB PNG: (n * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255 per axis, x right, y up, z toward the viewer, background (128, 128, 255)

path.description: when given, the PNG is written here instead of returned inline, honored by hosts with filesystem access and refused typed elsewhere (mirrors hew.doc.export)

scene.description: a Scene's id: renders through its resolved camera and hidden sets (Document::resolve_scene) instead of the document's own — falls back to the usual cameraless resolution when the Scene captures no camera. Mutually exclusive with camera and view. The Scene's section plane, if any, is NOT rendered headlessly at 1.0.

view.description: a named standard view fitted to the scene bounding box; mutually exclusive with camera and scene

width.description: defaults to 512; out-of-range values are clamped, not refused

result.description: two shapes depending on whether path was given: bytes base64 inline (default), or a path plus a sidecar path for each extra pass asked for (id-buffer, depth, normals)

depth_far.description: with a depth pass: the farthest drawn surface

depth_near.description: with a depth pass: meters from the eye, along the view axis, of the nearest drawn surface

depth_path.description: present only when include_depth and path were both given: "<path>.depth.png"

depth_png_base64.description: present only when include_depth was true and path was not given

id_buffer_base64.description: present only when include_ids was true and path was not given: u16 little-endian per pixel, index into id_palette (0 = background)

id_buffer_path.description: present only when include_ids and path were both given: "<path>.ids.bin", the same u16 little-endian per-pixel encoding written to disk

id_palette.description: public ids; id_palette[i] is what the id-buffer (inline or on disk) reports as index i+1

normals_path.description: present only when include_normals and path were both given: "<path>.normals.png"

normals_png_base64.description: present only when include_normals was true and path was not given

path.description: present only when path was given: echoes it back

png_base64.description: present only when path was not given

methods.summary: Set the app's displayed length-unit format (app/src/settings/units.ts's LengthFormat) — an app-level display PREFERENCE, never document state or file-format data.

format.description: metric: m, cm, mm; imperial: arch (feet+inches, e.g. 5' 3-1/8"), frac_in (fractional inches), dec_in (decimal inches)

methods.summary: Frame all visible geometry in the live viewport (View > Zoom Extents). A view effect, not a document edit (mutates_document = false).
